newsitem.title: UK: Forwarder ASG aims for top ten position.
newsitem.headline: Forwarder ASG aims for top ten position.

text.p: Sweden's ASG AB has embarked on an expansion programme aimed at establishing itself as one of the top 10 global freight forwarders over the next five years, said its UK sales and marketing manager Brad Brennan.

He told Reuters that the first stage of this plan, already underway, was to reaquire key overseas subsidiaries in the United States, the UK and the Far East that were sold to management buy-out teams four years ago.
Secondly, the company is looking to open new subsidiaries, or set up joint ventures in a number of areas where it is not represented, notably Malaysia, Korea, Indonesia, South America and India.

"When ASG decided on the overseas MBO course in 1993, it did so because at the time it wanted to focus on its Scandinavian origins. The idea then was to enter into an alliance for global business with Danzas," said Brennan.
"The company subsequently decided to expand itself internationally and the first step in this direction was to buy back ASG U.S. last summer."
Brennan added that the repurchase from the former MBO owners of ASG UK had just been completed, although he declined to disclose the price paid.

"The next aim is to buy back ASG's Far East operation, which covers Hong Kong (the Asia headquarters), China (where it has 12 offices), Vietnam, Taiwan, Singapore, Thailand and Japan. No sell back agreement has yet been reached but dialogue with the owners is continuing," he said.
Brennan said that since the MBO in the UK, the subsidiary's annual turnover had increased by 300 percent to reach 23 million stg in 1996.

ASG UK books space each week night on chartered Boeing 727 freighter services from East Midlands airport to Copenhagen, which connect with onward overnight flights to Oslo, Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmo and Helsinki and with trucking services to other points in Scandinavia.
At weekends, scheduled Scandinavian Airlines System flights are used from London Heathrow to Copenhagen, said Brennan.
ASG UK's main customer was Volvo, for which it transports to Sweden for final assembly UK-built components, mainly for the manufacturer's Volvo 858 model.
Brennan claimed ASG was responsible for 42 percent of the total airfreight market from the UK to Sweden. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
